themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 540% increase (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting rapid deterioration of street tree maintenance across Crown Heights, potentially creating safety hazards and blocking sight lines.
evidence: 4 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% spike, z-score 4.85)
Concurrent spike in illegal tree damage complaints: 9 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average (279% increase, z-score 4.43)
New tree requests also spiked: 8 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (2033% increase, z-score 10.96), indicating residents are requesting replacements
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance backlog in CD 308 and whether budget constraints are delaying trimming
Document specific locations where overgrown branches are creating safety or visibility issues; photograph hazards and talk to residents in affected areas

themes_detail.label: Noise from Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about noise from houses of worship exploded to 4 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 11.72, the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset)—indicating a sudden, acute conflict between religious institutions and neighbors.
evidence: 4 noise complaints from houses of worship last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% spike, z-score 11.72—highest anomaly in dataset)
Crown Heights has significant religious diversity; this spike suggests a new conflict or event triggering complaints
No prior pattern of complaints at this level, indicating a sudden change rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Identify which house(s) of worship are generating complaints; determine if a specific event, service schedule change, or renovation triggered spike
Interview complaining residents and house of worship leadership to understand the nature of noise and whether ongoing mediation is possible

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—signaling potential safety and accessibility risks in multi-unit buildings across the district, particularly affecting elderly residents and people with disabilities.
evidence: 3 elevator complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Concurrent spike in maintenance/facility complaints: 32 last week vs. 6.6 weekly average (383% increase, z-score 4.26), suggesting broader building infrastructure issues
Long-standing community board budget request for 'other facilities' suggests infrastructure has been under-resourced historically
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings have reported elevator failures; check DOB filings for maintenance permits or violations at those addresses
Interview residents in affected buildings about duration of outages and impact on mobility; talk to building management about maintenance budgets and contractor availability

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints (missing signs) spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1,100% increase (z-score: 4.16)—coupled with a maintenance/facility spike (32 complaints last week vs. 6.6 average, +383%), indicating accelerating deterioration of public space infrastructure.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% spike, z-score 4.16)
32 maintenance/facility complaints last week vs. 6.6 weekly average (383% increase, z-score 4.26), suggesting systemic upkeep failures
Community board's recurring budget request for 'other cleaning requests' to Department of Sanitation reflects ongoing maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Map locations of missing street signs; determine if particular intersections or neighborhoods are disproportionately affected
File FOIL request with DOE and Parks Dept. to understand maintenance schedules and staffing levels; interview residents about visibility and navigation impacts

themes_detail.label: Homelessness / Street Assistance Surge
themes_detail.summary: Requests for assistance with homeless persons spiked to 19 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 4.4 per week—a 334% increase (z-score: 5.35)—indicating a sudden rise in visible homelessness or street encampments, concurrent with long-standing community board requests for homeless facilities.
evidence: 19 homeless person assistance complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (334% spike, z-score 5.35)
Community board has made repeated annual requests for 'other facilities for homeless' to Department of Homeless Services, indicating the district perceives a need
Timing (3 weeks ago) suggests this may be cooling, but warrants verification of current street conditions
reporting_angles: Canvass Prospect Heights and Crown Heights parks, major intersections, and subway stations to document current visible homelessness; compare to baseline from 3 weeks ago
Interview Department of Homeless Services about shelter capacity, outreach resources, and service gaps in CD 308; talk to local nonprofit providers
